title: 仙佛合宗語錄 (Xianfo hezong yulu): 'the yang light appears' as the sign for stopping the fire
author: Wu Shouyang 伍守陽 (Wu Chongxu 伍沖虛)
edition_cited: Punctuated transcription on zh.wikisource (nine-chapter arrangement plus Q&A sections; no print edition named). A differently arranged Daozang jiyao recension (Kanripo KR5i0066), which I also opened, lacks the 'second and third appearance' wording.
tradition: Longmen neidan; founder text of the Wu-Liu school
locator_hints: Chapter 火足候止火景采大藥候天機第四: Q 'when the yang light appears, where does it appear?' A 'between the two eyebrows, the Bright Hall ... like a flash of lightning; this is the empty room bringing forth white'

Same chapter: first appearance during refining of essence (keep firing); complete 300 cycles, enter stillness and 'wait for the second appearance'; second = stop the fire; third = gather the great medicine; firing on to a fourth appearance loses the medicine
Chapter 七日采大藥天機第五: for seven days use 'the light of the two pupils', by day gazing at the middle field and by night keeping it there; 'the mechanism is in the eyes'
Chapter on the great medicine and Q&A sections: six signs including golden light in the eyes
summary: Wu Shouyang's question-and-answer manual is the earliest source found here for the Wu-Liu teaching that a light seen between the eyebrows times the alchemical work. He says the yang light appears at the 'Bright Hall' between the brows, 'like a flash of lightning', and identifies it with the empty room bringing forth white. A first flash comes during the refining of essence and the firing continues; when the three hundred cycles are complete the adept sits in stillness and waits; the second flash, together with genital retraction, means stop the fire; the third means the great medicine can be gathered; to keep firing until a fourth is to lose it. Gathering then uses the 'light of the two pupils' turned on the middle field for seven days. Light is never sought directly; it reports the state of the accumulated energy.
why_relevant: Primary instruction stating where and how the light is seen, how many times, and exactly what the practitioner must do at each appearance; shows the tradition treating seen light as a timing signal and attaching a danger to mishandling it.

date_evidence.basis: Wikisource header gives author 伍沖虛 and period 明 but names no edition. The same work is in the Daozang jiyao (Kanripo KR5i0066, base edition CK-KZ, the Chongkan Daozang jiyao reprint of 1906; year from my memory of that edition), which fixes a pre-1929 publication record for the work, though that recension's wording differs.

found_via: own lead (Wu-Liu 'three appearances of yang light'), zh.wikisource
notes: The reading agent should cite the Wikisource text for the three-appearance passage; I confirmed by search that the Daozang jiyao recension does not contain the strings 陽光二現 or 三現. No public-domain English translation found. Anchors: see ANCHOR RULE in the source file.
